description: Risk R-B first, because the class name inverts the behaviour: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN01C is TransactionAddController, and this program adds nothing - it VIEWS. Four independent artefacts say so: app/cbl/COTRN01C.cbl:5 'Function    : View a Transaction from TRANSACT file', README.md:314 '| CT01 | COTRN01 | COTRN01C | Transaction View |', app/bms/COTRN01.bms:2 'CardDemo - Transaction View' and the on-screen literal INITIAL='View Transaction' at POS=(4,30) - app/bms/COTRN01.bms:75-79. The mapset corroborates it structurally: 56 DFHMDF entries, 21 named, and exactly ONE UNPROT - TRNIDIN at :85 - which is a lookup-then-display screen and not a data-entry screen. Rule R1 resolves the conflict - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure, so it is documented here and never silently corrected. On THIS path the misleading name is dangerous in its sharpest form: the dataset the lookup addresses is NOT OPEN, so there is nothing to read and nothing to create. An unopened dataset is reported, never written to, and a controller called Add must not answer an unusable dataset by inserting the record it could not fetch. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion, the adapter verifies on every case that no mutating repository method was reached, and the three seeded rows - one of which carries the very key that was asked for - are pinned unchanged afterwards. The half of the swap that genuinely ADDS a transaction is COTRN02C, and its cases live in parity/COTRN02C. WHAT THIS CASE PINS: the WHEN OTHER arm of EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at app/cbl/COTRN01C.cbl:289-295, reached from the REENTER plus DFHENTER path by a condition that is GENUINELY RESIDUAL - DFHRESP(NOTOPEN), CICS response 19, which common.FileStatus classifies as Outcome.OTHER and which maps to NO named two-character FILE STATUS at all. That is the whole point of the case and it is the last of the three WHEN OTHER cases in this folder. case10 supplies the outcome FileStatus names END_OF_FILE and maps to the batch status '10'; case11 supplies DUPLICATE and '22'; this case supplies a value that has no such mapping, which is the strongest available demonstration that the arm is a true catch-all rather than a three-value enumeration written to look like one. common.FileStatus makes the distinction explicit rather than incidental: its named statuses are '00', '04', '10', '22' and '23', its Outcome.OTHER constant is the one Outcome built with no batch status at all - it stands for every value the programs did not enumerate - and FileStatus.cicsRespOfBatchStatus translates only '00', '10' and '23' in the reverse direction, so 19 is unreachable from any status name. Read the other way, FileStatus.outcomeOfCicsResp names 0 as OK, 20 as END_OF_FILE, 13 as NOT_FOUND, 14 and 15 as DUPLICATE, and returns Outcome.OTHER for everything else, 19 included. GATE G47 IS COMPLETED HERE, AND COMPLETED HONESTLY. The gate asks that every FileStatus and RESP outcome - '00', '10', '22', '23' and other - be driven per call site. COTRN01C has exactly ONE I/O call site: the keyed EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278. Its EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :280 has exactly THREE arms and no more: DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :281, DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :283 and WHEN OTHER at :289. Across the folder those three arms are now driven by six cases: case08 reaches the first with DFHRESP(NORMAL) and the '00' outcome; case09 and case05 reach the second with DFHRESP(NOTFND) and '23'; case10, case11 and this case reach the third, with the '10'-mapped outcome, the '22'-mapped outcome and a residual unmapped one respectively. All five outcomes the gate names are therefore covered, and NOT ONE BRANCH THE COBOL DOES NOT HAVE WAS INVENTED to get there. A keyed READ cannot report end-of-file or a duplicate as a distinct COBOL branch - there is no browse to run off the end of and no alternate key to duplicate - so '10' and '22' legitimately COLLAPSE into WHEN OTHER, and a not-open dataset was never going to have a branch of its own either. The collapse is stated openly rather than papered over (practice B12), and no fourth arm is added to the evaluation: the gate is satisfied by proving each outcome reaches its CORRECT arm, because a fabricated branch would satisfy the letter of a checklist while asserting a control flow the source does not have (practice B4 - document, never invent). THE TRACE, statement by statement. :88-92 sets ERR-FLG-OFF and USR-MODIFIED-NO and blanks WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO. EIBCALEN is 218, so :94 takes its else arm and :98 copies the passed area over CARDDEMO-COMMAREA. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at 1, so CDEMO-PGM-REENTER already holds at :99 and control takes the ELSE at :110-111 - which is why the echoed context is still 1 and why the :100 SET, the :101 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COTRN1AO and the :102 MOVE -1 never run. :111 performs RECEIVE-TRNVIEW-SCREEN (:230-238), then the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :112 takes its FIRST arm, WHEN DFHENTER, and performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. The EVALUATE TRUE at :146 takes its SECOND arm - TRNIDINI is populated, so it is neither SPACES nor LOW-VALUES - and that arm is MOVE -1 TO TRNIDINL (:154) followed by CONTINUE, with no message and no send. WS-ERR-FLG is therefore still 'N', so :158 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is TRUE: the thirteen detail items are blanked in source order at :159-171 (TRNIDI, CARDNUMI, TTYPCDI, TCATCDI, TRNSRCI, TRNAMTI, TDESCI, TORIGDTI, TPROCDTI, MIDI, MNAMEI, MCITYI, MZIPI), :172 moves TRNIDINI into TRAN-ID and :173 performs READ-TRANSACT-FILE. The read at :269-278 states DATASET (WS-TRANSACT-FILE) INTO(TRAN-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-RECORD) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) UPDATE RESP RESP2, and reports DFHRESP(NOTOPEN). The EVALUATE at :280 therefore falls past both named arms to WHEN OTHER, whose five statements run in this exact order: DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD (:290), MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG (:291), MOVE 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' TO WS-MESSAGE (:292-293), MOVE -1 TO TRNIDINL (:294) and PERFORM SEND-TRNVIEW-SCREEN (:295). Control returns to the END-IF at :174, and :176 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is now FALSE - a second test rather than an ELSE - so the thirteen record-to-screen moves at :177-190 and the send at :191 are SKIPPED. The task ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of :136-139. THE MAP IS SENT EXACTLY ONCE. The unconditional PERFORM SEND-TRNVIEW-SCREEN at :109 belongs to the first-entry arm and is unreachable from the :110-111 else arm, so on the REENTER path the only send is the rejecting one inside the read. case05 reaches its arm from :103-107 and then falls through to :109, which is why its fingerprint carries two sends; a fixture asserting two sends here would be describing that case rather than this one, and the count is behaviour rather than bookkeeping. ALL THIRTEEN DETAIL FIELDS ARE SPACES, not LOW-VALUES and not record data: they were blanked at :159-171 before the read and the error flag then blocked :176, so nothing ever repainted them. That is the whole observable behaviour of a failed lookup - an empty form and a message - and it is the assertion that catches a translation which reported the failure and painted the record anyway. TRNIDINO retains the requested id, because COTRN1AO REDEFINES COTRN1AI so the received TRNIDINI occupies the same sixteen bytes and no arm of this path clears them. THE DISPLAY LINE, BYTE-EXACT - the distinguishing assertion of this case. :290 is DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD, and it is the ONLY DISPLAY statement in all 330 lines of the program, confined to this one arm. The two literals are exactly 'RESP:' and 'REAS:' - five characters each including the colon, with NO space after either colon - and they are reproduced character for character. WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD are both PIC S9(09) COMP (:43-44), and DISPLAY of a binary item renders it at its declared digit positions, so each operand is exactly NINE digits, zero-filled on the left, and the whole line is 5 + 9 + 5 + 9 = 28 characters with no separator anywhere. The pinned pair is RESP 19 and RESP2 60, and both values are named rather than left implicit: 19 is common.FileStatus.NOTOPEN, the CICS DFHRESP(NOTOPEN) raised against a dataset that is not open, and 60 is the RESP2 the IBM CICS Application Programming Reference documents for NOTOPEN on a file control command. DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D), so both numbers are reproduced from that documentation in common.FileStatus rather than read from a DFHRESP copybook this checkout does not contain - the same provenance the DFHENTER mnemonic in common.CicsAid has. The rendering is therefore 'RESP:000000019REAS:000000060', and a reviewer can check the arithmetic from the two declarations alone (practices B8 and B12). THE PAIR DIFFERS FROM BOTH SIBLINGS IN BOTH COMPONENTS, which is the entire diagnostic value of a third case: case10 renders 'RESP:000000020REAS:000000000' and case11 'RESP:000000015REAS:000000000', so the three residual cases are told apart on the one channel that exists to tell them apart. Neither component is 0 for RESP - that is DFHRESP(NORMAL) and belongs to case08 - and neither is 13 - that is DFHRESP(NOTFND) and belongs to case09 and case05. Both values are PINNED CONSTANTS and neither is derived from anything run-variant (practice B7). EXACTLY ONE ENTRY carries this DISPLAY, and it is the ONLY entry on the DISPLAY_LINE channel. It is ORDERED THIRD rather than first, and the position is a fact about the fingerprint rather than a preference: the recorder reports WS-MESSAGE at its declared PIC X(80) first, ERRMSGO at its declared PIC X(78) second, and every DISPLAY after them, and the differ compares emitted lines POSITIONALLY and on their declared channels. Placing an 80-byte expectation opposite a 28-character observation would compare across channels of different widths, which is precisely the comparison the channel model exists to prevent, so the DISPLAY is stated where it is emitted in the fingerprint - matching case10 and case11 exactly - and its uniqueness is asserted by there being one of it. THE ERROR MESSAGE, BYTE-EXACT. The literal at :292-293 is 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' - lower-case 'lookup', capital 'T' in 'Transaction', three trailing dots - reproduced character for character with no normalisation, and identical to case10 and case11 because the source reuses one literal for EVERY WHEN OTHER outcome. NO 'dataset not open' wording is substituted: the program has none, and inventing a more informative message would be a behaviour change (practice B5). It is thirty-one characters, and it is asserted on both channels at their own widths because :217 moves WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) into ERRMSGO PIC X(78) and COBOL discards the two rightmost bytes: WS_MESSAGE_80 carries the literal followed by 49 spaces and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 the same literal followed by 47, both counted mechanically rather than by eye (practice B11). This is not either of the program's other two message literals and must never be confused with them: case09 and case05 report 'Transaction ID NOT found...' from :285-286, case06 reports 'Tran ID can NOT be empty...' from :149-150, and case17 and case18 report CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY from :130. All three are distinct, and only this one accompanies a DISPLAY. THE SEEDED RECORDS, AND WHY ONE OF THEM CARRIES THE REQUESTED KEY. TRANSACT has no ASCII fixture - app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine files and none is a transaction master - so the rows are declared inline and no tenth fixture is invented. Seeding no rows at all would have been defensible for a not-open dataset, and it was rejected deliberately: the three rows are the same three case10 and case11 seed, differing only in the middle row's self-describing TRAN-DESC narrative, so the only BEHAVIOURAL variable across the three residual cases is the condition the read reports, and that is what makes a difference between them attributable. Row 1 IS the requested id 0000000000001002. The record the operator asked for is PHYSICALLY PRESENT, and the read still reports an unusable dataset, so the run must take WHEN OTHER, emit the DISPLAY, leave the thirteen detail fields blank and send once. A translation that answered from the data it could see instead of from the condition the read reported - or that treated a response which is neither NORMAL nor NOTFND as recoverable and retried, or opened the dataset itself and read again, or fell back to a browse - would paint 1002's thirteen fields and fail on every one of them at once. 0000000000001001 and 0000000000001003 bracket it one below and one above, so a repository that fell to a neighbouring record would also be caught. Each row is 350 bytes, summed mechanically from the fourteen spans of app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy (practice B11): TRAN-ID X(16) 1-16, TRAN-TYPE-CD X(02) 17-18, TRAN-CAT-CD 9(04) 19-22, TRAN-SOURCE X(10) 23-32, TRAN-DESC X(100) 33-132, TRAN-AMT S9(09)V99 133-143, TRAN-MERCHANT-ID 9(09) 144-152, TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) 153-202, TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) 203-252, TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) 253-262, TRAN-CARD-NUM X(16) 263-278, TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26) 279-304, TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) 305-330 and FILLER X(20) 331-350. The FILLER is present and space-filled (gate G21): it is a span rather than a gap, and omitting it would leave every row 330 bytes. TRAN-AMT occupies ELEVEN bytes - nine integer digits and two fractional, scale 2 (gate G23) - with the sign OVERPUNCHED into the trailing byte 143 and never carried in a twelfth byte or a leading sign position: '0000010011A' is +1001.11 because A is the positive overpunch for 1, '0000010022B' is +1002.22 because B is the positive overpunch for 2, and '0000010033L' is -1003.33 because L is the negative overpunch for 3. PIC X spans are space-padded and PIC 9 spans zero-filled. Both timestamps of every row are PINNED 26-byte literals in the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmmmmm shape - 4+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+6 = 26 - and never a captured 'now' (practice B7). None of the record content is ever painted on this path, which is the assertion; the projection of a record that IS painted is case08's subject. TRANSACT'S FINAL STATE IS PINNED UNCHANGED, and that is an assertion rather than bookkeeping. :275 states the UPDATE option, so a completed read would take a record lock, and a translation that took a lock and then rewrote or deleted the record would be caught here and nowhere else in the response. A read against a dataset that is not open has nothing to write back. The repository returns the failure as a DISCRIMINATED OUTCOME carrying the status with its RESP and RESP2 and NEVER abends on the caller's behalf, which is what lets the COBOL's own EVALUATE structure survive the translation unchanged; an exception would have unwound past :176 and lost the second test altogether, and the DISPLAY with it. The not-open condition is expressed through those values and not as a thrown error, deliberately. It is also worth stating what a not-open dataset IS here: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:76-87 defines FILE(TRANSACT) with STATUS(ENABLED) and OPENTIME(FIRSTREF), so the file opens on first reference rather than at startup, and IBM documents the CLOSED and UNENABLED state NOTOPEN reports as one a file can be defined into or driven into by a CLOSE. The condition is therefore ENVIRONMENTAL rather than a program error, and it is not modelled as one: no abend, no retry, no write and no bespoke diagnostic is added. The keyed read is a READ ... UPDATE that never rewrites, and the repository correctly declares no rewrite and no delete for TRANSACT (practice B5). THE HIGHLIGHT, and a finding this fixture records rather than invents. Gate G38 asks that the CSSETATY error highlight apply only in REENTER state. This case is REENTER AND in error, which is the combination in which a highlighting screen would highlight - and COTRN01C still applies none, because it has no highlighting to apply. The program's eight COPY statements at :52, :63, :65, :66, :67, :69, :71 and :72 are COCOM01Y, COTRN01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA: CSSETATY is NOT among them, the source contains zero occurrences of DFHRED and no FLG-<field>-NOT-OK pair for a resolver to act on, and no attribute byte is moved anywhere in its 330 lines. COTRN01C therefore satisfies G38 in the strongest available form - no highlight in EITHER state - and 'attributes' is present and EMPTY rather than absent, which is the positive statement that the decision was taken through the same FieldAttributeSetter the highlighting screens use and came back untouched. Pinning DFHRED and a '*' on TRNIDIN would assert an attribute byte this program never writes, on a path where it never writes it, and that is exactly the invention practice B4 forbids; it is also unaddressable, because app/cpy-bms/COTRN01.CPY declares only the xxxL, xxxF, xxxA and xxxI items per field and no xxxC, xxxP, xxxH or xxxV item exists in it to carry such a value. METADATA IS NOT PAYLOAD. The xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items are length, flag and attribute metadata and never payload members, which is why none of them appears among the twenty-one fields. TRNIDINL is the metadata item that matters here: -1 is moved into it twice on this path, at :154 and again at :294 - two of the six sites in the program, the others being :102, :151, :287 and :311 - and -1 in an xxxL item is the CURSOR request, so it is reported once as cursorField exactly as AAP section 0.3.9 requires. STATELESSNESS (rule R6, gate G37): the whole 218-byte area travels in the payload and nothing is held server-side. app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy is 34 + 84 + 12 + 16 + 14 = 160 bytes and the CDEMO-CT01-INFO extension at :53-61 is 16 + 16 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 16 = 58, which is 218 in all; the 58-byte extension is carried as its own field rather than folded into the 160-byte context all seventeen controllers depend on, and all 22 fields are pinned so none is left unchecked. The AID travels in the payload too. The case supplies a realistic re-entry - the operator arrived from CT00/COTRN00C on page 1 of a browse spanning 1001 to 1003, selected 1001, and has now typed 1002 over the field - and every one of those values comes back exactly as it arrived, because no arm of this path writes a CDEMO- field. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT remains 1. CDEMO-CT01-TRN-SELECTED carries 0000000000001001 deliberately: it is read only at :103-107 inside the first-entry arm and must NOT be consulted here, because :172 keys the read from the TYPED TRNIDINI, so a translation that reached for the commarea selection instead would be keying 1001 and not 1002. A field the passed area does not name keeps what its picture gives it, spaces for PIC X and zeros for PIC 9. NAVIGATION AND TERMINATION. There is NO EXEC CICS XCTL on this path, so no transfer target is invented and the XCTL of :205-208 stays unreached - which is why gate G40 is not asserted here. nextProgram nonetheless carries COTRN01C, and that is not a transfer: the task ends at EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:429-430 binds TRANSACTION(CT01) to PROGRAM(COTRN01C), so the operator's next input returns to this same program and the response says so rather than leaving the client to guess. nextMapset and nextMap carry the COTRN01 and COTRN1A that the SEND at :219-225 names, and termination is RETURN_TRANSID. THE RETURN CODE IS 0, AND ON THIS CASE THAT IS THE LEAST OBVIOUS AND MOST IMPORTANT ASSERTION IN THE FILE. A dataset that will not open is the closest COTRN01C comes to a fatal condition, and it is tempting to expect a non-zero code for it. The source does not give one: COTRN01C contains ZERO CALL 'CEE3ABD' sites and ZERO occurrences of RETURN-CODE anywhere in its 330 lines, so no input whatsoever can make it abend. It reports the error on the screen and ends normally at :136-139, and gate G35 does not apply to this program at all. Every one of the twenty cases in parity/COTRN01C therefore asserts expectedReturnCode 0, and this is the case where that fact is least self-evident. No abend expectation is stated and no non-zero exit appears anywhere in this fixture, because inventing one would turn a reported failure into a terminated task. THE HEADER SIX come from POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :243-262 and are identical on every send this program makes. TITLE01O is CCDA-TITLE01 PIC X(40) from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-19 and TITLE02O is CCDA-TITLE02 PIC X(40) from :22 - the ACTIVE line, because :21 is COMMENTED OUT in the copybook and carries the superseded 'Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)' text that must not be used. Neither is COTTL01Y's X(40) CCDA-THANK-YOU at :23-24, and neither is CSMSG01Y's X(50) CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU at :18-19; the two thank-you items are different widths in different copybooks and are not interchangeable. TRNNAMEO is WS-TRANID 'CT01' X(04) and PGMNAMEO is WS-PGMNAME 'COTRN01C' X(08), both from :36-37. CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are built from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :245 and are therefore the one part of the screen a wall clock would make irreproducible, so the clock is PINNED at 2022-07-19T23:12:34 - the timestamp the source's own version footer at :329 carries, 'Date: 2022-07-19 23:12:34 CDT' - giving CURDATEO '07/19/22' from WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and CURTIMEO '23:12:34' from WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS. The same pinned pair is used by case01 through case11, so a header difference between sibling cases can only mean a difference in the header logic (practice B7). The twenty-one field widths come from the symbolic map's xxxI PICTURE clauses in app/cpy-bms/COTRN01.CPY - TRNNAME 4, TITLE01 40, CURDATE 8, PGMNAME 8, TITLE02 40, CURTIME 8, TRNIDIN 16, TRNID 16, CARDNUM 16, TTYPCD 2, TCATCD 4, TRNSRC 10, TDESC 60, TRNAMT 12, TORIGDT 10, TPROCDT 10, MID 9, MNAME 30, MCITY 25, MZIP 10 and ERRMSG 78 - and every one was measured programmatically rather than typed by eye. BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED, by structured reading of MAIN-PARA, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, READ-TRANSACT-FILE, SEND-TRNVIEW-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts (app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy), the BMS field contract (app/cpy-bms/COTRN01.CPY and app/bms/COTRN01.bms) and the file and transaction definitions in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:76-87 and :429-430. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, which AAP section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers, and the change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. No user rules were provided for this project - review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided.' and that single line is the whole document - so the AAP section 0.10.2 practices bind instead, and their absence is not treated as licence to lower the bar. GATES DISCHARGED: G15 (one of exactly twenty cases in parity/COTRN01C), G18 (the diff count must be zero, per module rather than per build), G19 (three 350-byte records, each pinned as a whole image so the total width is asserted), G21 (FILLER present and space-filled at 331-350), G23 (all three amounts are scale 2 with the sign overpunched into byte 143), G30 (both ordered EVALUATEs honoured in source order - EIBAID at :112 takes the first of its five arms, and WS-RESP-CD at :280 reaches WHEN OTHER only after DFHRESP(NORMAL) and DFHRESP(NOTFND) have both been tested and failed, with a response neither of them names, which is what makes WHEN OTHER genuinely last AND genuinely a catch-all rather than merely written last), G37, G38 (REENTER WITH error, and still no highlight, because this program has none), G47 (COMPLETED for this program: with case05 and case08 through case12 the single keyed read now drives '00', '10', '22', '23' and a residual other, each landing in the arm the COBOL sends it to and each reported as a discriminated value rather than an exception) and G51 (the controller is driven as a plain object, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path). Deliberately NOT asserted, because this program or this path has none of them: G32 (zero GO TO in COTRN01C), G35 (zero CALL 'CEE3ABD' and zero RETURN-CODE, which is why the return code is 0 even for a dataset that will not open, and no abend is expected), G39 (no pagination), G40 (no XCTL on this path) and G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC). COTRN01C performs no arithmetic at all - zero ADD, SUBTRACT, COMPUTE, MULTIPLY and DIVIDE - and ROUNDED appears zero times in it as in all 28 programs, so any scaling is RoundingMode.DOWN by rule R2. Dead working storage is left exactly as it stands (practice B5): WS-USR-MODIFIED at :45-47 is set at :89 and never tested again, and WS-TRAN-DATE PIC X(08) VALUE '00/00/00' at :50 is never referenced at all; neither is asserted, and neither is tidied away.
